l4_steps.name: Analyse seasonal schedule demand vs slot inventory
l4_steps.input: Approved seasonal schedule build, prior-season slot inventory
l4_steps.output: Slot gap analysis report identifying constrained O&D pairs
l4_steps.kpi: Slot gap identification rate ≥95% before coordinator submission deadline
l4_steps.pain_point: SkyCAST demand forecasts do not auto-reconcile with live coordinator slot libraries — manual cross-check required, introducing errors in high-frequency bank builds

l4_steps.name: Classify constrained airports by IATA Level 2 / Level 3
l4_steps.input: Slot gap analysis report, OAG airport level classification data
l4_steps.output: Constrained airport register with Level 2/3 designation and coordinator contact
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of Level 3 airports correctly classified before coordinator submission window opens
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA airport level classification updates lag real-world congestion changes by up to one season; misclassification causes incorrect submission routing and missed deadlines

l4_steps.name: Generate prioritised slot request register
l4_steps.input: Constrained airport register, route profitability data from SkyCAST
l4_steps.output: Prioritised slot request register ranked by revenue impact
l4_steps.kpi: Slot requests submitted ≥8 weeks before IATA coordination deadline
l4_steps.pain_point: Late submission forfeits priority queue position at 47% of Level 3 coordinators; SkyWORKS has no built-in deadline tracking for each coordinator's unique submission calendar

l4_steps.name: Extract historical slot series from IATA CRS portal
l4_steps.input: Prior-season SSIM files, coordinator portal access credentials
l4_steps.output: Historical slot series inventory per airport with series reference codes
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of historical series extracted before coordinator portal submission window closes
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA CRS portal availability falls below 99.5% during peak submission windows; fallback is manual email-based SSIM exchange with no automated validation

l4_steps.name: Validate 80/20 utilisation rule compliance per series
l4_steps.input: Historical slot series inventory, actual operations data from prior season
l4_steps.output: Series compliance report with used/available ratio per airport per series
l4_steps.kpi: Grandfather right retention rate ≥98% of eligible series per IATA WSG
l4_steps.pain_point: Operational disruptions (weather, ATC) erode utilisation ratios; airlines must file force majeure exemptions within 5 days of each triggering event — SkyWORKS does not auto-flag breaches in real time

l4_steps.name: File force majeure exemptions for at-risk series
l4_steps.input: Series compliance report, confirmed disruption log with ATC/weather evidence
l4_steps.output: Accepted exemption filing per affected slot series
l4_steps.kpi: Exemption filed within 5 calendar days of triggering disruption event
l4_steps.pain_point: Missed exemption window results in permanent series loss with no appeals mechanism at most Level 3 airports; coordinator acceptance rates vary by region (EU coordinators accept ~82%, US FAA exempt)

l4_steps.name: Generate SSIM-formatted SCR slot request messages
l4_steps.input: Prioritised slot request register, validated historical series inventory
l4_steps.output: SSIM SCR message set ready for coordinator submission
l4_steps.kpi: SSIM file validation error rate < 1% on first submission
l4_steps.pain_point: SkyWORKS SSIM export requires manual field mapping for airports not in the standard IATA airport list; common source of format errors that delay acceptance by coordinator systems

l4_steps.name: Submit slot requests to each airport coordinator
l4_steps.input: SSIM SCR message set, coordinator portal credentials per airport
l4_steps.output: Submitted SCR messages with coordinator receipt confirmations
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of requests submitted before each coordinator's unique deadline
l4_steps.pain_point: Airport coordinators (ACNUSA, NATS, DFS, FAA, etc.) each operate different portal UIs with no single API standard; multi-airport submissions require manual portal navigation per coordinator

l4_steps.name: Evaluate initial slot allocation vs requested schedule
l4_steps.input: Coordinator SCT (slot confirmation) messages, original slot request register
l4_steps.output: Allocation gap report identifying unmatched or partially matched requests
l4_steps.kpi: Allocation match rate ≥85% of requested slots in initial SCT response
l4_steps.pain_point: Coordinators allocate on grandfather-then-new-entrant priority; late filers receive only residual slots, which are frequently at off-peak times incompatible with planned bank structures

l4_steps.name: Prepare negotiation brief for IATA slot conference
l4_steps.input: Allocation gap report, network simulation scenarios from SkySYM
l4_steps.output: Negotiation brief with ranked alternative slot windows and revenue impact estimates
l4_steps.kpi: Brief finalised ≥2 weeks before IATA slot conference opening date
l4_steps.pain_point: SkySYM scenario export does not auto-generate slot swap proposals; analyst must manually map network simulation outputs to coordinator slot pool data, taking 3–5 days per conference cycle

l4_steps.name: Negotiate slot swaps and alternatives at conference
l4_steps.input: Negotiation brief, coordinator available slot pool published at conference
l4_steps.output: Agreed slot swaps or confirmed alternative allocations
l4_steps.kpi: ≥70% of critical slot gaps (top 10 revenue routes) resolved at conference
l4_steps.pain_point: Bilateral swap negotiations are blocked when the counterparty airline holds conflicting grandfather claims on the same series; coordinator cannot force swaps without both parties' consent under IATA WSG §9

l4_steps.name: File appeal for unresolved critical slot gaps
l4_steps.input: Unresolved slot gap list post-conference, coordinator appeal process documentation
l4_steps.output: Formal appeal filing or coordinator mediation request
l4_steps.kpi: Appeal response received within 5 business days of filing
l4_steps.pain_point: Appeal panels have no binding authority at most coordinators; outcomes are advisory only, leaving airlines with no recourse if coordinator declines to intervene in grandfather disputes

l4_steps.name: Confirm final slot allocation and accept coordinator offer
l4_steps.input: Final SCT messages from all coordinators including post-conference revisions
l4_steps.output: Accepted slot confirmation records per airport per series
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of confirmed slots acknowledged within 24h of coordinator receipt
l4_steps.pain_point: Coordinator systems deliver SCT messages in overnight batch files; missed or delayed messages require manual reconciliation with coordinator helpdesk, often taking 2–3 business days to resolve

l4_steps.name: Integrate confirmed slots into SkyWORKS schedule build
l4_steps.input: Accepted slot confirmation records, current SkyWORKS seasonal schedule
l4_steps.output: Updated SkyWORKS schedule with slot-validated departure and arrival times per flight leg
l4_steps.kpi: Schedule-to-slot reconciliation accuracy ≥99.5% before SSIM publication
l4_steps.pain_point: Slot times and SkyWORKS schedule times drift due to timezone and DST mapping errors during SSIM import; DST boundary airports (e.g. LORD, EIDW) are a recurring source of off-by-one-hour faults

l4_steps.name: Publish season SSIM file to GDS channels and PSS
l4_steps.output: Published SSIM file distributed to Sabre GDS, Travelport GDS, Amadeus GDS, and Amadeus Altéa PSS
l4_steps.kpi: SSIM distributed to all GDS ≤72h after final coordinator confirmation
l4_steps.pain_point: GDS distribution from SkyWORKS is fire-and-forget with no real-time ACK; distribution failures are silent and only detected when downstream booking discrepancies surface 24–48h later

l4_steps.name: Monitor weekly slot utilisation against 80% threshold
l4_steps.input: Weekly actual operations data, slot series inventory with coordinator reference codes
l4_steps.output: Weekly slot utilisation compliance report per series per airport
l4_steps.kpi: Slot series utilisation ≥80% per IATA WSG standard throughout season
l4_steps.pain_point: Operational cancellations and schedule swaps erode utilisation without triggering automated alerts in SkyWORKS; compliance analysts must run manual SQL queries against ops data to compute rolling utilisation ratios

l4_steps.name: Return or swap underperforming slot series
l4_steps.input: Utilisation compliance report identifying series below 80%, coordinator return deadlines
l4_steps.output: Slot return confirmations or approved swap records per series
l4_steps.kpi: Slot returns submitted ≥48h before departure per IATA WSG in-season return deadline
l4_steps.pain_point: Late returns are forfeited to the slot pool with no recovery; repeated late-return flags accumulate as coordinator penalty records that reduce priority scoring in subsequent season bids

l4_steps.name: Execute ad-hoc slot swaps for operational recovery
l4_steps.input: Operations disruption report, coordinator available slot pool for swap
l4_steps.output: Ad-hoc swap confirmation and updated slot record in SkyWORKS
l4_steps.kpi: Ad-hoc swap processed within 2h of disruption notification during coordinator office hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Coordinator swap availability is limited to office hours (typically 07:00–19:00 local); out-of-hours disruptions at Level 3 airports have no swap mechanism, forcing cancellation or slot violation
